extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and communications/PR professionals interested in advertising and cultural controversies
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or creating corporate advertising (TV/online spots) for cultural sensitivity and reputational risk, especially when referencing protest movements or charged social issues. Focuses on avoiding appropriation, misrepresentation, and backlash and on appropriate crisis response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid appropriation of protest movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads should not appropriate or use nationwide protest movements to sell products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article: critics accused Pepsi of "appropriating a nationwide protest movement following police shootings of African Americans." Anti-pattern: using imagery or narratives from ongoing social movements as a marketing device without meaningful connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not trivialize urgent social issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising must not diminish the seriousness or urgency of the issues depicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted criticism: "This ad trivializes the urgency of the issues and it diminishes the seriousness and the gravity of why we got into the street in the first place." Avoid upbeat, lighthearted framing that downplays real harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reenacting or exploiting iconic protest imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not recreate or mimic widely recognized images of real protests or individuals who suffered harm without careful consideration and permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article notes many believed the final scene referenced the photograph of Ieshia Evans. Anti-pattern: staging scenes that closely mirror real-life moments of trauma or detention for commercial ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray protests accurately, not as sanitized caricatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent demonstrations and activists authentically rather than as smiling, break-dancing, or superficially cheerful groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article observation: "It's not clear what the smiling, attractive demonstrators are upset about" — portraying protesters as vague, pleasant extras undermines real causes and invites criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid savior narratives that center privileged figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not position privileged celebrities or consumers as the neutralizing/solving force for others' struggles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opening line critique: imagining a protest "led by a 21-year-old white supermodel" suggests a savior dynamic. Anti-pattern: casting a privileged actor as the solution to systemic injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align brand messaging with social context and avoid tone-deaf positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure campaign themes and brand slogans are appropriate given current social conversations and power dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pepsi described the spot as reflecting "today's generation" and "Live For Now"; the article implies this positioning clashed with the gravity of the topics used. Test whether brand voice fits the issue depicted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologize for harm and address affected communities specifically
rubrics_metrics.description: If a campaign causes offense, apologies should acknowledge harm, speak to those affected, and not be limited to statements of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activist DeRay McKesson criticized Pepsi's apology for failing to apologize to "the people who dedicated their lives and their time to these issues." Anti-patterns: generic corporate apologies that focus on 'missing the mark' without acknowledging harm or stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not focus apology on intent; acknowledge impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate statements should prioritize acknowledgement of impact over explanations of lack of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pepsi's statement began "We did not intend to make light of any serious issue," which was portrayed as insufficient. Guidance: center the harmed community and the consequences rather than intent alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult with represented communities when depicting struggles
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage people and organizations connected to the movements or communities portrayed during concepting and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While implied rather than explicit, the article's criticisms (appropriation, misrepresentation) support involving stakeholders to avoid missteps. Example safeguard: seek feedback from activists or community leaders before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and test for social media backlash and satire
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how potential audiences will react online; anticipate parody, satire, and rapid viral criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article shows immediate Twitter mockery and satire following the ad's release. Guidance: run sensitivity/readership testing and simulate likely user-generated responses for campaigns touching on contested topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to remove content and halt rollout if necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Have crisis-response plans to pull content and stop distribution quickly when a campaign generates significant, justified backlash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pepsi "removed the content and halting any further rollout" after condemnation. Guidance: a swift, concrete action to prevent further harm is an expected part of crisis management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider historical precedents but evaluate current sensibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Past advertising that used counterculture or protest imagery does not guarantee acceptability today; assess historical analogies against modern contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article references Coca-Cola's 1971 'I'd Like to Teach the World to Sing' as a precedent but implies modern reactions and power dynamics differ. Guidance: don't rely on past successful examples as proof a similar approach is acceptable now.
